+ACCEPT the bounded reentrant keyboard release ownership repair at `be746ec811b98365c378609ca936502783bb106d`, paired with renderer `0d2aaf964b31d4191a76cf84900d7433b4611fa4`. No production defect was found in the assigned scope. This task independently validates retained evidence and makes the final acceptance decision; the interrupted predecessor did not finish publication.
+
+| Evidence | Result |
+|---|---|
+| Unchanged independent rejection fixture, review `372eb7de549492021520db38c3c51459ab4d982d` | 7 PASS reused |
+| Retained new actual-renderer reentrant challenges | 7 PASS reused |
+| Cross-layer cancellation / ownership / timeline / focus transfer / legacy | 12 + 6 + 3 + 3 + 1 PASS reused |
+| Bridge-release and renderer-keyup rejecting controls | Both exit 1 at the intended downstream release assertion |
+| Exact original cross-layer fixture `cd3ce6e221c50d34df92dcad0c2b14b6ef99b2d0` | Rejects repaired browser at its immutable older-browser hash assertion, before cases |
+| Accepted renderer receipt | 46 manifest payloads rehashed; 119 cases plus legacy reused |
+
+The ten retained groups in `retained-checkpoint.json` were all completed before the predecessor's model-capacity failure. This task rehashed every group's fixture, stdout and stderr, validated expected case counts and assertion text, and checked all pinned source files against their exact Git revisions and blobs. No completed group was rerun. The later coordinator messageboard clarification expressly confirmed reuse of all retained groups. The copied predecessor decision draft was excluded; this is this task's decision. `reuse-validation.json` and `retained-validation.json` record verification.
+
+The browser SHA-256 is `5b2c47fa0b901f0323bc04df34ff27d8c50e47a001d77e9dcae3f2986a3477f0`; renderer SHA-256 is `209e06f67ec38940ecab071890a296e665500e43a52b9bd96abd4ec90fccf304`. `pins.json` binds the renderer require closure and original fixtures. Production source is unchanged by this task.
+
+The repair's relevant locations in `lib/browser-input.js` are lines 1100–1116 (snapshot ownership records, check identity, delete before calling UP, finish draining after exceptions, propagate first error), 1138–1145 (publish DOWN ownership before renderer delivery and stop stale continuation), and 1166–1175 (normal UP uses and removes captured ownership). These locations agree with the observed DOWN/UP order and cleared physical/delivered state. The predecessor draft's shifted line references were corrected here.
+
+The seven new cases call actual installed renderer key methods and drain the real input queue. They challenge repeated hide/blur from the renderer wake callback; modeled detachment followed by body-target UP; detachment plus hidden cancellation with both Shift sides held; throwing wake hooks; UP wake reentry with another held key; a throwing queue publisher after DOWN; and two-key cancellation with throwing publishers and first-error propagation. Renderer wake-hook exceptions are swallowed by its actual implementation; publisher exceptions propagate after state/queue updates. The tests verify exactly one release per owned key, no stale release, and cleared physical and delivered held state. Detachment is bounded DOM scaffolding (`isConnected=false`, activeElement moves to body); it is not engine-level node removal and removal alone is not claimed to cause cancellation. Arbitrary renderer exceptions before a state transition are outside this guarantee.
+
+The original cross-layer fixture supports `BROWSER_INPUT_SOURCE` and `RENDERER_INPUT_SOURCE`, but independently pins browser `2b5eaa0` at line 17. Its actual repaired-source invocation and initial rejection are retained in `crosslayer-unmodified.*`. The separately named `test/keyboard-focus-renderer-repaired-pin-oct26.test.cjs` changes only the exact browser SHA-256 literal; `crosslayer-pin-only.patch` and byte equality verification prove all 25 behavioral assertions and both targeted rejecting controls are unchanged. This is supplemental repaired-source acceptance, not a pass of the immutable original fixture. No assertion was removed, broadened or weakened. Both controls reject at `exactlyOneRelease`, line 157, with `release must reach renderer delivery exactly once`.
+
+Original failing parent/candidate evidence and the supplied baseline remain byte-identical in `original-*`; they were compared to the original independent-review donor and were not recreated. The old narrow reproducer reported a stranded physical key after hidden cancellation; the unchanged seven-case acceptance now reports DOWN then UP and cleared physical state. Repair-owner supplied19/scoped6 results remain provenance only, not new independent results.
+
+Historical aggregate low-bit behavior is unchanged. The three known aggregate consume-before-delivery failures remain explicitly retained in `renderer-aggregate-known-limitation.log`; cross-layer legacy rearming is one of the 25 passing cases. The source-identical renderer closure and its accepted 119+legacy receipt were reused without rerunning them.
+
+Recovery uses installed Node serially: `timeout 25s node --max-old-space-size=16 FIXTURE`. Supply `BROWSER_INPUT_SOURCE` pointing to the exact repaired browser and `RENDERER_INPUT_SOURCE` to the exact renderer with `mem-utils.js` and `region-map.generated.js` alongside it. For the unchanged seven-group fixture, use its exact bytes in a small isolated test/lib layout with that renderer closure in `../lib`; it does not use the renderer environment override. The two retained new fixtures are published under `test/`. For the cross-layer fixture select `FOCUS_INTEROP_GROUP=cancellation`, `ownership`, `timeline`, `focus-transfer`, or `legacy-contract`. Rejecting controls select `negative-control` and additionally `FOCUS_INTEROP_NEGATIVE=bridge-release` or `renderer-keyup`; require exit 1 and the intended assertion. Original commands, absolute retained paths, per-case checkpoints and hashes remain in `retained-checkpoint.json`. No handwritten implementation clone is used.
+
+The resource gate was measured before checkout, review and publication. Readonly flat donor object stores and installed tools are standing inputs, not copied history. Current shared WAL bytes are conservatively charged once in full because no launch-time all-WAL baseline was supplied, with 12 MiB future growth and 8 MiB reserve. All owned checkout/Git, ops, launcher/session and evidence bytes are included. No mounts or guest command exist, so filename-bearing mount parsing is inapplicable; the trusted supplied SSH configuration is retained unchanged. Runtime argv confirms fresh Sol 6.1 medium, 200000 total compaction; actual compaction was not exercised.
+
+Remaining gates: coordinator review; authorized current-main integration and merged regressions; real browser focus/removal behavior; guest/runtime qualification. No main integration, build, browser or runtime claim is made. No box was assigned or touched: ID/state/expiry N/A; lifecycle ownership stays with the coordinator. No workers were spawned, services changed, or production files edited. Stop after verified task-branch publication.
+
+Publication review: full `git diff --cached --check` reports exactly six whitespace-only lines in the byte-preserved historical renderer aggregate failure log (18, 20, 37, 39, 58, 60). They are retained to preserve its original hash. The remaining staged paths pass the whitespace check; no fixture or production whitespace exemption was added. This routine packaging finding does not change acceptance.
